title: Floating Buildings
objective: After this level you can explain how buildings can float on water.
summary: A floating house sinks until the water it pushes aside weighs as much as it does. Maasbommel's amphibious houses sit on hollow concrete bases and rise on mooring posts; in 2011 they floated.

cards.headline: In 2011, a Dutch river rose, and the houses on its banks rose with it.
cards.body: At Maasbommel in the Netherlands, 32 amphibious houses and 14 floating ones were built in 2004 and 2005 outside the river dikes. In 2011 the River Maas rose high enough for the amphibious houses to float for the first time. No problems were found. So how does a house built on concrete float?

cards.headline: Archimedes moves in
cards.body: A floating object sinks until the water it pushes aside weighs as much as it does; then the water's upward push holds it up. That's why a lump of clay sinks but the same clay shaped into a boat floats, and why steel ships float too. Shape does the work. So each amphibious house at Maasbommel stands on a large, hollow concrete cube: plenty of room to push water aside.

items.label: Floating
points: A relatively light timber frame on top

items.label: Both
points: Slide up and down steel mooring posts
Can rise and fall up to 5.5 m

cards.fact: Carry in a piano, and the house sits lower.
cards.context: Level 2's load path ended in the soil. A floating house's path ends in water: the house settles until the water it displaces weighs as much as the house and everything in it. Add a live load, like Level 2's piano, and it sinks a little deeper until the balance returns. Floating homes keep the heavy concrete below and build light on top.

cards.headline: Floating buildings: launched
learned: A floating object displaces its own weight of water
Hollow concrete bases float, like a clay boat
Amphibious houses rest on land until floods lift them
Maasbommel's houses floated in 2011, as designed

options.rationale: They floated right where they stood.

questions.explanation: In 2011 the river rose high enough for the amphibious houses to float for the first time, and no problems were found.

questions.prompt: Why can a house on a hollow concrete base float?

options.label: Concrete is lighter than water
options.rationale: A solid lump would sink; the hollow shape does the work.

options.label: Steel posts hold it up above the river
options.rationale: The posts guide it; the water holds it up.

options.label: It pushes aside water weighing as much as it does
Air pumps keep lifting it from below

questions.explanation: A floating object sinks until the water it displaces weighs as much as it does, like a clay boat or a steel ship.

questions.prompt: Level 2 calls a piano a live load. What happens when one is carried into a floating house?

options.label: Nothing: floating houses ignore live loads
options.rationale: Every added load changes the balance.

options.label: The house rises slightly
options.rationale: Extra weight pushes it down, not up.

options.label: The house settles a little lower in the water

questions.explanation: The house sinks a little deeper until the water it displaces again weighs as much as the house and its contents.
